clue.text: Back to the old 6d piece of course!

indicators.note: Back tells the solver to read the whole run of letters that follows in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
6d is sixpence in pre-decimal British money: VI for six and D for penny (Latin denarius)

explanation.surface: A nostalgic cry for an old sixpenny item, apparently a golfing souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6d' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down, but it is old British money, sixpence, written VI D. TO + VID read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clump of turf hacked out by a golf club is a familiar bit of the golf course.

clue.text: Planking supplied by Birdwood

definitions.meaning: a waterbird followed by a piece of timber, read as a compound

explanation.surface: Boards are provided by a man named Birdwood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birdwood' looks like a surname but is a cryptic second definition: a bird (DUCK) plus wood (BOARD). 'supplied by' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Slatted boards laid over mud in trenches form a walkway of planking.

clue.text: River noted for boatmen

parts.note: the famous Russian folk song about men hauling barges, the Song of the boatmen of a great Russian river

explanation.definitionFit: The Russian river is famed through the folk song about its barge haulers.

clue.text: In the main they help some to feel for others

definitions.text: In the main they help some to feel for others

parts.words: In the main they help some to feel for others
parts.note: the main is the sea, and some sea creatures use long limbs to feel around for prey

explanation.definitionFit: Octopuses and squid use these long feelers to grope for food.

clue.text: State of affairs in office?

definitions.meaning: the circumstances one finds oneself in
a post or job, an older sense of the word

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how things stand at the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a set of circumstances and a job or post, as in 'situations vacant'.

clue.text: Actor's aim, in a way — to fill most parts

indicators.note: to fill means these letters go inside the other group
parts suggests the word is split up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: An actor aims, in some fashion, to take on most of the roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges MOST into STOM, and A RD ('a way') fills it. 'in' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame and celebrity as a leading performer is what an aspiring actor dreams of.

clue.text: Cradle rocker — oak finish ?

parts.note: the nursery rhyme has a baby's cradle rocked by the wind at the top of a tree, and an oak ends at its crown

explanation.definitionFit: In the lullaby 'Rock-a-bye baby' the cradle sits at the very crown of a tree.

clue.text: Can this be for ever ? Must be a stop soon

definitions.meaning: alludes to the novel Forever ... by Kathleen Winsor
the traffic light that warns drivers red is coming

explanation.surface: A worried lover asks whether this can last, fearing the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forever Amber' was a famous 1940s historical romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the novel Forever Amber, and the traffic-light colour signalling a halt imminent.

clue.text: Conceiving one master-spirit in German leader

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MA is the degree Master of Arts
gin is an alcoholic spirit
taken as written

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of the word German

explanation.surface: One mastermind is dreaming up plans inside a German chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master-spirit' looks like one compound but splits into MA and GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceive something is to form it in the mind, to picture it.

clue.text: Tend to give rail union directions

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen in Britain
S and E are the compass points south and east

explanation.surface: A railway union is inclined to issue instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tend to' looks like 'be inclined to', but 'Tend' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To look after the sick or care for someone is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stop Dane getting involved in an architectural row

parts.note: a colon is a punctuation mark, a stop

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters becoming tangled up together into a new order

explanation.surface: A Dane is told to halt as he wanders into a line of buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting involved' rearranges DANE into NADE, after COLON.
explanation.definitionFit: A row of columns supporting a roof or entablature is a classic architectural feature.

clue.text: Pound returned to look for Orwell, really

indicators.note: returned asks for those letters to come back the other way

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound weight
an air is a look or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone searches for Orwell's earnings, sincerely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns LB into BL. Eric Blair was the real name of the writer George Orwell, hence 'really'.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair, so his real surname is meant.

clue.text: Master Swahili

parts.note: the Swahili word used for a master or boss, a form of address in East Africa

explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa this term was the respectful address for a master or sir.

clue.text: Resolve to hinder men one replaced

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or hinder

indicators.note: replaced means these letters are put back in a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A commander decides to obstruct soldiers being swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges MEN plus I into MINE, which follows DETER.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve on something is to decide it firmly, a synonym.

clue.text: A cloudy morning seen from a cave 4 ac

parts.note: dull weather is overcast and cloudy

explanation.surface: A grey morning viewed from inside a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 across is SITUATION, so the definition reads 'a cave situation'. In the Bible David hid in the Cave of Adullam, and the name became a byword for a refuge of malcontents.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Cave of Adullam where David took refuge gives this place name, a cave location.

clue.text: Last word in diplomacy

parts.note: the final demand before negotiations break off, after which force follows

explanation.definitionFit: A final set of terms whose rejection ends talks is the diplomat's closing statement.

clue.text: Contractors could arrange sea-trip

indicators.note: could arrange invites the letters to be sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Builders might organise a cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SEA-TRIP are rearranged. 'Contractors' looks like builders but means those who enter into a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: The signatories to a contract are known legally as the parties to it.

clue.text: Golf ?

parts.note: golf is played in eighteen-hole circuits, so it is a sport of circuits

explanation.definitionFit: Golf is played as a circuit of holes, making it a sport of circuits.

clue.text: Trapper's weapon ?

parts.note: a firearm set to discharge when an animal or intruder trips a wire

explanation.definitionFit: A firearm rigged to fire automatically via a tripwire, used against poachers or game.

clue.text: Hates appearance of foreign matches

parts.note: de is French for of
tests are international cricket matches

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the look of overseas sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: Test matches are the long international games of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe someone is to abhor them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Settle for transport to be up before eleven

indicators.note: in a down clue, to be up means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: a bus is a form of transport
a side is a team, eleven in cricket or football

explanation.surface: Someone accepts the travel arrangements for an early-morning team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be up' writes BUS upwards as SUB. 'before' joins it to SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that sinks or floodwaters that recede are said to sink down or settle.

clue.text: Perhaps one bathing machine part

definitions.meaning: someone who dives into the water, a diver
a piston or rod that moves up and down in a pump or similar

explanation.surface: A swimmer is perhaps part of a bathing machine on a Victorian beach.
explanation.walkthrough: A bathing machine was a wheeled hut used on Victorian beaches, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes a dive into the sea, and also a piston in a pump or syringe.

clue.text: Excuse made before writing, perhaps

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
text is an example of writing

explanation.surface: An apology is drafted before writing it down.
explanation.definitionFit: A false reason given to hide the real one is a cover story, a synonym.

clue.text: Journeyman's assistant'?

parts.note: a journeyman is read as a traveller, and the thing that helps one is a schedule of departures

explanation.definitionFit: A traveller relies on a printed schedule of departures and arrivals.

clue.text: Change holders of farms ?

definitions.meaning: cash drawers in shops that hold coins
cultivates the soil, works the land

explanation.surface: Someone wants to alter who owns the farms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change holders' reads as a verb phrase but is the coin drawers of a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash registers hold the change, and ploughing the land is what a farmer does to it.

clue.text: Roots entangled with trunk

indicators.note: entangled says the letters are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: A tree's roots are wrapped around its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests a tree, but it is the human body without limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The human body without head or limbs is called the trunk.

clue.text: Endlessly deceiving Poe detective

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: duping is deceiving or tricking

explanation.surface: A ceaselessly misleading sleuth from Edgar Allan Poe.
explanation.walkthrough: Endlessly drops the G from DUPING.
explanation.definitionFit: C. Auguste Dupin is Edgar Allan Poe's amateur sleuth, the fictional investigator of the Rue Morgue.

clue.text: Break up about one, showing signs of ill-feeling

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: to snap is to break
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A broken-off relationship leaves someone showing resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SNAP into PANS, and 'about' wraps it round I. 'ill-feeling' suggests resentment, but here it is physical aches.
explanation.definitionFit: Aches are what a person feels when unwell, physical discomfort.

clue.text: Subsequently found to be dead right

parts.note: the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: Someone is afterwards shown to be absolutely correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right' reads as 'quite correct' but splits into dead (LATE) and right (R).
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards or at a following time is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Repeating it for instance about the train accident

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation goes round what follows

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation for for example

indicators.note: accident suggests the letters have crashed into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone keeps describing a rail crash, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' rearranges TRAIN into RATIN, which 'about' puts inside EG, after IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something again and again is to repeat it, a synonym.

clue.text: Sleepy order given to Pole in yachting area

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Solent is the strait off the Isle of Wight famous for sailing
OM is the Order of Merit
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: A drowsy instruction is given to a Polish sailor off the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent, between the Isle of Wight and Hampshire, is a famous yachting stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsy, inclined to doze, is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Some helpless Englishman in a German city ?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A helpless Englishman finds himself stranded in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large industrial city in the Ruhr, western Germany.
